title: Venn Diagrams, HCF & LCM
summary: Pupils meet the Venn diagram with no numbers at all, put the prime factors of two numbers into a Venn, then read the HCF (multiply the middle) and the LCM (multiply everything) off it. Heavy scaffold, with support taken away one step at a time. Every question is authored and its answer computed.

els.text: I can put things in the right part of a Venn diagram.

•  Say what each circle is for
•  Put a thing in both circles when it fits both
•  Put a thing in neither when it fits neither

slides.title: Model: match the tiles one for one

els.text: Model: match the tiles one for one

Mei puts all three 2s of 8 in the middle, because 2 is in both numbers.

Where does it go wrong?
The right circle should multiply to 12. Hers is 2 × 2 × 2 × 3, which is too big. Only the 2s both numbers have go in the middle.
How many 2s should go in the middle for 8 and 12? 2

items.title: Who is right about $54$ and $80$?
question: Who is right?
answer: Ben is right: the middle holds only the tiles both numbers have. $80$ has no $3$, so only a $2$ goes in the middle.
explanation: The middle is for tiles in both numbers.

claims.name: Mei
claims.text: $54 = 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3$ and $80 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5$. I put a $2$ and a $3$ in the middle, because $3$ is a factor of $54$.

claims.name: Ben
claims.text: Only a $2$ goes in the middle. A tile goes in the middle only if both numbers have it, and $80$ has no $3$.

options.reasoning: Puts a tile in the middle that only one number has. The middle is only for tiles in both numbers.
$80$ has no $3$, so a $3$ in the middle makes the right circle multiply to a different number from $80$.

misconception.label: Puts a tile in the middle that only one of the two numbers has, instead of only the tiles both numbers have

items.title: Can the middle be empty?
question: Who is right?
answer: Amara is right: $27$ is all $3$s and $32$ is all $2$s, so nothing is in both. An empty middle is a correct answer.
explanation: Nothing is in both, so nothing goes in the middle.
The left circle multiplies to $27$ and the right circle to $32$.

claims.name: Leo
claims.text: $27 = 3 \times 3 \times 3$ and $32 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ share no tile, so the middle is empty. I must have made a mistake.

claims.name: Amara
claims.text: The middle is empty because $27$ and $32$ share no prime. That is fine: some pairs of numbers share nothing.

options.reasoning: Thinks two numbers must always share a tile, so an empty middle has to be a mistake.
If the empty middle were a mistake, the circles would have to multiply to something other than $27$ and $32$. They do not.

misconception.label: Thinks an empty middle must be a mistake, because two numbers always share something
